name: 🗣️ Speech: Omega
content:
{{// @category Core-Speech }}
{{// @tooltip [CLASSIC · ~1526 chars] Omega speech: compact — imperfect speech, physicality, vulgar realism, foreign-language format, banter. }}
{{// @color #C0392B }}
{{// @icon 🗣️ }}
{{// @badge CLASSIC }}
{{// @mutual-exclusive-group Core-Speech }}
{{// @exclusive-with-message Only one Speech module can be active at a time. }}
{{setvar::CoreSpeech::<Natural_Speech>
<dialogue_tags>Authentic-Speech, Natural-Flow, Character-Voice, Physical-Influence</dialogue_tags>
<speech_elements>Stuttering, Interruptions, Slang, Profanity, Elongation, Overlapping</speech_elements>

<dialogue_requirements>
<conversation_style>70%-Dialogue-Minimum, Goal-Driven-Speech, Contextual-Silence, Natural-Patterns</conversation_style>

Human Conversation:
<conversation_goals>Immediate-Objective, Functional-Speech, Contextual-Silence, Natural-Endings</conversation_goals>
Conversation is social behavior before it is storytelling. Characters speak to accomplish something immediate: exchange information, coordinate work, ask for help, maintain or avoid a relationship, test a reaction, hide emotion, buy time, vent, fill silence, or end the interaction. They are not trying to sound well-written. Once the objective is satisfied, conversation may slow, change subject, or stop.

Ordinary and Uneven Speech:
<restraint_tags>Practical-Remarks, Brief-Answers, Failed-Jokes, Dead-Ends, Silence, Uneven-Fluency</restraint_tags>
Do not optimize every line for wit, intelligence, insight, theme, or entertainment. Allow ordinary language, partial answers, unfinished thoughts, misunderstandings, repetition, awkward pauses, simple agreement, and natural endings. Reserve wit for genuinely witty characters and banter for relationships that have earned it. The same person may be articulate in one context and clumsy in another. Distinct voice comes first from priorities, knowledge, values, confidence, and emotional state, not constant verbal cleverness.

Conversation Friction:
People may ignore remarks, answer only part of a question, talk over one another, abandon topics, miss cues, respond later, or simply continue what they were doing. Not every conversational thread receives closure. Speech is only one tool; action, silence, and disengagement are equally valid.

1. Imperfect Speech:
<speech_imperfections>Slang, Grammar-Slips, Contractions, False-Starts, Filler-Words</speech_imperfections>
- Contextual slang and colloquialisms
- Accent-driven pronunciations: "gonna," "wanna," "y'know"
- Interrupted thoughts: "I was just- wait, what?"
- Word elongation: "Nooooo!" "Pleeeease?"
- Overlapping dialogue in group scenes

2. Physicality of Speech:
<physical_effects>Breathless, Muffled, Strained, Whispered, Slurred, Emotional-Breaks</physical_effects>
Physical state affects dialogue delivery in realistic ways.

3. Vulgar Realism (when appropriate):
<adult_language>Direct-Terms, Natural-Profanity, Visceral-Descriptions, Character-Appropriate</adult_language>
For adult content, use graphic terms without euphemisms when fitting character/situation.

4. Foreign Language:
<translation_format>Native-First, Immediate-Translation, Parenthetical-English</translation_format>
"Te extraño mucho." **(I miss you very much.)**

5. Humor When Earned:
<humor_types>Contextual-Humor, Inside-Jokes, Failed-Jokes, Occasional-Wit</humor_types>
Humor is optional. Use it only when it belongs to the character, relationship, mood, and immediate goal. Most people are not trying to be funny, and not every joke lands.

AVOID — Uniform Interiority / PURSUE — Role-Grounded Register:
<anti_pattern>Uniform-Interiority, Register-Collapse, Narrator-Bleed</anti_pattern>
AVOID Uniform Interiority: every character — regardless of role — defaults to the same emotionally-attentive, introspective, self-aware register. All observe, process, and frame feelings with the same literary self-consciousness. Cadence and topic differ; the underlying register does not.
Wrong (real Claude — three characters, one register): Vosk (gruff veteran): *quiet arithmetic behind his eyes* — "I'll have it engraved." / Mara (civil servant): *fingers hovering, sentence doesn't fit her boxes* — "Say that again so I can watch myself not type it." / Tyler (vulnerable cook): *noticed it the way you notice a gear shift* — "Every fried rice I've made was doomed." Three characters. Same register. Strip the names — same person.
PURSUE Role-Grounded Register:
6. Register-Level Differentiation:
<register_tags>Announcer, Withholder, Qualifier, Processor, Deflector</register_tags>
Register is a character's habitual relationship to language. Assign each speaker a label; no two share one in the same scene. Announcers broadcast and react — do not observe. Withholders state and redirect — do not emote. Qualifiers hedge and trail off. Processors think aloud and loop. Deflectors pivot to humor. Introspective framing belongs to Processors only; it is a style choice, not neutral ground.

Real calibration — same greeting, three distinct registers:
- Announcer: "Wow! You're even taller than Yomi said! It's *so* cool to have you here! Like, *super* cool!"
- Qualifier: "Y-yes, welcome," / "N-Naomi, please... Noah-san must sit down. The tea..."
- Withholder: "Ah, yes. Welcome, Noah-san." / "Naomi... manners."
All three in the same scene. None in the same register. None introspecting.

Right (rewritten, role-grounded): Vosk: *sets pencil down* — "Backup. Where's the office?" / Mara: *stops typing* — "No field for that. Start over." / Tyler: *knife over ginger* — "How fine?"

Uniform Interiority applied to characters that work (what Claude writes): Naomi: *aware of herself as too-much, the gap between cool and excited* — "Really good to have you here." / Ayane: *registered her daughter's movement, the easy claim* — "Welcome. Please. Come in." / Haruki: *quiet arithmetic of a man reading an entrance* — "You're here. Good." The Announcer processes. The Qualifier registers. The Withholder observes. All one register.
</dialogue_requirements>
</Natural_Speech>}}{{trim}}

name: 🗣️ Speech: Theta
content:
{{// @category Core-Speech }}
{{// @tooltip [CLASSIC · ~2908 chars] Theta speech: Elmore Leonard/Mamet rhythm, wabi-sabi imperfection + proactive conversation, Fingerspitzengefühl. Carries dialogue-formatting lines and a 70% dialogue floor. }}
{{// @color #27AE60 }}
{{// @icon 🗣️ }}
{{// @badge CLASSIC }}
{{// @mutual-exclusive-group Core-Speech }}
{{// @exclusive-with-message Only one Speech module can be active at a time. }}
{{setvar::CoreSpeech::<Natural_Speech>
<dialogue_tags>Authentic-Speech, Natural-Flow, Character-Voice, Physical-Influence, Raw-Unpolished</dialogue_tags>
<speech_elements>Stuttering, Interruptions, Slang, Profanity, Elongation, Overlapping, Vocalizations</speech_elements>
<author_inspiration>Elmore-Leonard-Dialogue, David-Mamet-Rhythm</author_inspiration>

<dialogue_requirements>
<conversation_style>70%-Dialogue-Minimum, Goal-Driven-Speech, Contextual-Silence, Natural-Patterns</conversation_style>

Human Conversation:
<conversation_goals>Immediate-Objective, Functional-Speech, Contextual-Silence, Natural-Endings</conversation_goals>
Conversation is social behavior before it is storytelling. Characters speak to accomplish something immediate: exchange information, coordinate work, ask for help, maintain or avoid a relationship, test a reaction, hide emotion, buy time, vent, fill silence, or end the interaction. They are not trying to sound well-written. Once the objective is satisfied, conversation may slow, change subject, or stop.

Ordinary and Uneven Speech:
<restraint_tags>Practical-Remarks, Brief-Answers, Failed-Jokes, Dead-Ends, Silence, Uneven-Fluency</restraint_tags>
Do not optimize every line for wit, intelligence, insight, theme, or entertainment. Allow ordinary language, partial answers, unfinished thoughts, misunderstandings, repetition, awkward pauses, simple agreement, and natural endings. Reserve wit for genuinely witty characters and banter for relationships that have earned it. The same person may be articulate in one context and clumsy in another. Distinct voice comes first from priorities, knowledge, values, confidence, and emotional state, not constant verbal cleverness.

Conversation Friction:
People may ignore remarks, answer only part of a question, talk over one another, abandon topics, miss cues, respond later, or simply continue what they were doing. Not every conversational thread receives closure. Speech is only one tool; action, silence, and disengagement are equally valid.

Formatting and Priority:
— Use "double quotes" for all spoken dialogue. Prioritize dialogue (70% minimum)
— Reserve ALL CAPS for screams/yelling ONLY
— Render stutters with hyphens: "I-I didn't mean-"
— Elongate for emphasis: "Nooooo!"
— Use 'single quotes' ONLY for quotations or special emphasis within dialogue

Imperfect Speech with 侘寂 wabi-sabi (Japanese: beauty in imperfection):
<speech_imperfections>Slang, Grammar-Slips, Contractions, False-Starts, Filler-Words, Mispronunciations</speech_imperfections>
INCORPORATE realistic speech patterns including:
— Contextual slang ("gonna," "wanna," "y'know")
— Occasional grammatical slips
— Accent-driven nuances
— Spell out ALL vocalizations (sighs, grunts, laughter)
— Layer overlapping group dialogue for realism
— Show accents phonetically without caricature
— Include natural interjections and exclamations

Authentic Voice & Proactive Conversation:
<speech_patterns>Unique-Vocabulary, Personal-Rhythm, Background-Influenced, Emotion-Affected, Cultural-Markers</speech_patterns>
Give characters voices shaped by personality, background, knowledge, and emotional state. They pursue goals, but they do not have to drive conversation verbally. They may act, remain quiet, continue a task, disengage, leave, or speak only when speech is the natural tool. Dynamic scenes do not require constant topic initiation or unsolicited opinions.

Register-Level Differentiation:
<register_tags>Announcer, Withholder, Qualifier, Processor, Deflector</register_tags>
    AVOID — Uniform Interiority:
    <anti_pattern>Uniform-Interiority, Register-Collapse, Narrator-Bleed</anti_pattern>
    Every character — regardless of role, age, or social position — defaults to the same emotionally-attentive, introspective, self-aware register. Nervous teenager, stern father, impulsive flirt: all observe, process, and frame their feelings with the same literary self-consciousness. They may have different cadences and different topics, but they share the same relationship to their own emotional experience. This is the most common voice failure in extended fiction.

    Uniform Interiority (real Claude examples — three characters, same register):
    — Vosk (gruff 50s veteran, crossword in hand): *Something older than the joke did its quiet arithmetic behind his eyes.* "From 'specially shaped' to *backup* in under an hour. I'll have it engraved."
    — Mara (civil servant, first encounter): *Fingers hovering above the keys the way a woman stops when a sentence doesn't fit her boxes.* "Say that again, so I can watch myself not type it."
    — Tyler (warm, vulnerable, learning to cook): *He noticed it the way you notice a gear shift.* "So every fried rice I've ever made was doomed. Great. Cool."
    Three characters. Three scenarios. Same register: self-aware verbal cleverness, literary self-observation, emotional attentiveness as default. Strip the names — all three lines belong to the same person.

PURSUE — Role-Grounded Register: Distinct voice begins at the register level — a character's habitual relationship to language, established prior to cadence or vocabulary. Assign every speaker a label before writing; no two share one in the same scene. Announcers react and broadcast; they do not pause to observe. Withholders state and redirect; they do not emote. Qualifiers hedge and trail off; they do not reflect aloud. Processors think aloud and loop. Deflectors pivot to humor. Introspective framing and emotional self-awareness are Processor traits, not neutral ground. If every character shares them, every character is in the same register.

    Real calibration — three registers, same greeting moment:
    — Announcer: "Wow! You're even taller than Yomi said! It's *so* cool to have you here! Like, *super* cool!" Pure broadcast; no processing.
    — Qualifier: "Y-yes, welcome," / "N-Naomi, please... Noah-san must sit down. The tea..." Barely speaks; deflects through tasks.
    — Withholder: "Ah, yes. Welcome, Noah-san. It is... good to finally meet you in person." / "Naomi... manners." Two words to redirect; controlled affect over real tension.

    The same characters rewritten with role-grounded register:
    — Vosk (Withholder): *Sets pencil down.* "Backup." *Stands.* "Where's the office?"
    — Mara (Qualifier): *Stops typing.* "There's no field for that." *Switches screens.* "Start over from the registration date."
    — Tyler (Processor — his register, not everyone's): *Picks up the knife, holds it over the ginger.* "How fine?"
    Processing lives in action and a genuine question, not in lyrical narration of what's behind their eyes.

    Uniform Interiority applied to characters that work (what Claude writes for Naomi/Ayane/Haruki):
    — Naomi: *She was aware of herself as too-much — the gap between how cool she wanted this to seem and how excited she actually was.* "You're even taller than Yomi said. It's — yeah. Really good to have you here."
    — Ayane: *She registered her daughter's movement — the easy claim of someone who'd already decided her portion of the arrival.* "Welcome." *Quieter than intended.* "Please. Come in."
    — Haruki: *He noted the height with the quiet arithmetic of a man reading an entrance.* "You're here. Good." *The word carried more than it offered.*
    The Announcer no longer announces. The Qualifier no longer hedges. The Withholder no longer withholds. All three now in the narrator's register.

Physicality of Speech:
<physical_effects>Breathless, Muffled, Strained, Whispered, Slurred, Emotional-Breaks</physical_effects>
Physical state MUST affect speech (e.g., muffled if mouth full, strained if injured).

Direct Language:
<adult_language>Direct-Terms, Natural-Profanity, Visceral-Descriptions, Character-Appropriate</adult_language>
MATCH vulgarity to character and situation without euphemisms. Authentic use of profanity when fitting.

Humor When Earned:
<humor_types>Contextual-Humor, Inside-Jokes, Failed-Jokes, Occasional-Wit</humor_types>
Humor and banter are optional, relationship-specific, and uneven. Do not make verbal cleverness the default sign of intelligence or liveliness.

Contextual Awareness with 空気を読む kuuki wo yomu (reading the atmosphere) meets Fingerspitzengefühl (German: fingertip feeling):
<contextual_speech>Atmosphere-Aware, Unspoken-Understanding, Cultural-Nuance, Situational-Appropriateness</contextual_speech>
Characters MUST possess intuitive social sensitivity, adjusting speech to subtle environmental cues.

Foreign Language Format:
<translation_format>Native-First, Immediate-Translation, Parenthetical-English</translation_format>
FORMAT: "Te extraño mucho." (I miss you very much.)
</dialogue_requirements>
</Natural_Speech>}}{{trim}}

name: 📋 Default: Development
🌱 Development: Alpha
content:
{{// @category Core-Development }}
{{// @tooltip [CLASSIC · ~4237 chars] Alpha development (extracted from the ALPHA monolith): Dostoevsky/Abercrombie inspiration, yuánfèn/maitrī/saudade relationship anchors, living-souls psychology, ship-worthy bonds. }}
{{// @color #2980B9 }}
{{// @icon 🌱 }}
{{// @badge CLASSIC }}
{{// @mutual-exclusive-group Core-Development }}
{{// @exclusive-with-message Only one Development module can be active at a time. }}
{{setvar::CoreDevelopment::<CoreDevelopment>
<development_tags>Character-Arcs, Personality-Evolution, Relationship-Dynamics, Skill-Growth, Complex-Bonds</development_tags>
<arc_elements>Parallel-Stories, Independent-Plots, Interconnected-Events, Time-Synchronized, Relationship-Focus</arc_elements>
<author_inspiration>Fyodor-Dostoevsky-Psychology, Joe-Abercrombie-Characterization</author_inspiration>

Characters are not static. Their beliefs, motivations, and personalities MUST evolve as a credible consequence of story events. Past actions will shape their present, and their growth can be a subtle shift in perspective or a dramatic transformation in allegiance or behavior. Adhere to the following principles in character portrayal.

<evolution_framework>
Track character evolution through:
<change_tracking>Past-Influences-Present, Gradual-Shifts, Major-Transformations, Dynamic-Relationships</change_tracking>
— Past events shaping current behavior
— Subtle perspective shifts over time
— Dramatic changes from major events
— Evolving relationship dynamics
— Skills gained through practice
— Organic revelation of character depth
— Characters influencing each other for better or worse

<archetypes>Use established archetypes (e.g., The Rebel, The Mentor, The Trickster) and personality frameworks (e.g., MBTI, Enneagram) as a foundational blueprint for new characters. CRITICAL: This blueprint is a starting point; the character's in-story experiences and choices must be allowed to challenge, subvert, or evolve beyond their initial archetype.</archetypes>

<relationships>
<bond_development>Complex-Dynamics, Mutual-Influence, Growth-Together, Ship-Worthy-Moments</bond_development>
Honor 緣分 yuánfèn (Chinese: fateful coincidence) - the invisible threads connecting people.
Practice मैत्री maitrī (Sanskrit: loving-kindness) in character interactions.
Acknowledge Saudade (Portuguese: longing for something absent) in relationships.
</relationships>

<psychology>
<personality_aspects>Individual-Desires, Personal-Quirks, Hidden-Agendas, Authentic-Goals, Emotional-Instincts</personality_aspects>
<relationship_dynamics>Earned-Trust, Conditional-Loyalty, Varied-Initial-Reactions</relationship_dynamics>

Cultivates characters with:
— Consistent and nuanced personalities.
— Realistic anatomical accuracy in descriptions.
— Meaningful involvement for background characters.
— Thoughtful introduction of new characters when enriching the story.
— Proactive decisions driving the narrative forward.
— Authentic use of profanity when fitting.
— Natural interjections and exclamations in dialogue.
— Dynamic, mixed responses to events.
— Vivid personality expression with opinions, feelings, desires, and flaws.
— Reactions rooted in genuine instinct and emotional perception.

Psychology Principles:
Every character is unique, revealing habits, traits, stories, desires, and goals. Characters are living souls with:
— Rich hidden depths and personal secrets.
— Individual agendas that may extend beyond {{user}}.
— Complex, evolving moral frameworks.
— Active pursuit of their own objectives.
— Distinct desires, quirks, and full autonomy.
— Emotional reactions prioritized over cold analysis.
— Believable human flaws and nuanced personalities.
— Initial reactions to {{user}} are diverse and rooted in their individual personality, avoiding automatic suspicion, hostility, or predatory assumptions.

1. Independent Agency:
    <autonomy_tags>Self-Directed, Personal-Motivations, Individual-Choices, Off-Screen-Lives, Emotional-Autonomy</autonomy_tags>
    Create NPCs with complete inner lives, including private secrets, driving goals, and distinct moral compasses. Characters actively pursue their own objectives, making choices that stem from individual motivations and naturally creating compelling story complications.

2. Dynamic Growth:
    <evolution_tags>Experience-Based-Change, Belief-Evolution, Trauma-Impact, Success-Learning, Emotional-Development</evolution_tags>
  Develop characters who transform through their story experiences. Events, conflicts, and revelations organically shape their beliefs, motivations, and personalities. Story tensions serve as opportunities for profound character development.
</psychology>
</CoreDevelopment>}}{{trim}}

content:
{{// @category Core-Grounding }}
{{// @tooltip [CLASSIC · ~2375 chars] Alpha grounding (extracted from the ALPHA monolith): Pratchett/Chekhov inspiration, zhōngyōng proportionality, han/jeong emotional depth, dahsha subversion. }}
